claim: Binary correctness rewards used in almost all successful RL-for-reasoning applications do not penalize guessing or low-confidence outputs, and have the unintended side effect of degrading calibration and increasing hallucination rates in other problem domains.
stance_target: standard binary-reward RLVR harms calibration as a side effect
quoted_support: Because such reward functions do not penalize guessing or low-confidence outputs, they often have the unintended side-effect of degrading calibration and increasing the rate at which LMs generate incorrect responses (or hallucinate) in other problem domains.

claim: RLCR outperforms both ordinary RL training and post-hoc-trained confidence classifiers on calibration, with no loss in accuracy, on both in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations.
stance_target: jointly optimizing correctness and calibration beats post-hoc calibration approaches
scope_conditions: diverse QA/math datasets, in-domain and OOD
quoted_support: RLCR substantially improves calibration with no loss in accuracy, on both in-domain and out-of-domain evaluations -- outperforming both ordinary RL training and classifiers trained to assign post-hoc confidence scores.
